title: Drake Shot Future’s ‘Ya Hit’ Video Scenes at Moody Center Without Permission, Rice University Says
summary: The college still welcomes the 6 God back to campus for another visit.
contentText:
Drake shot scenes from Future’s “Ya Hit” music video at Rice University’s “Twilight Epiphany” Skyspace installation by artist James Turrell at the Moody Center for the Arts, but reportedly never received proper permission to film the commercial work on campus.

According to Chron , Drizzy’s appearance on the Houston school grounds was unauthorized and campus security was left in the dark about the 6 God showing up.

“Neither the Moody Center for the Arts nor Rice University was aware of or involved in the production of Drake’s music video,” Rice’s executive director of news and media relations, Chris Stipes, told Chron . “While commercial filming on campus requires prior authorization, we recognize the broad appeal of the Rice Public Art Collection and welcome visitors to experience these remarkable works.”

However, the university isn’t pursuing any action against Drake for not securing permits and welcomes him back to the Moody Center for the Arts exhibits. “Drake, like all visitors, is welcome to return to campus to enjoy Rice’s public art,” Stipes continued.

Billboard has also reached out to Drake, Future and Rice University for comment.

Drake appeared alongside Travis Scott and Loe Shimmy on Future’s “Ya Hit,” which arrived on Nov. 6; a visual was shot in Houston before the release. Drizzy was the only one to make his way to Skyspace, while the entire crew reunited at nearby local favorite strip club Area 29. The video also included a scene from the OVO rapper’s 40th birthday festivities.

The collaboration marked the first between Future, Travis Scott and Drake, while they’ve worked separately with one another extensively. “Ya Hit” debuted at No. 38 on the Billboard Hot 100 and currently sits at No. 64.

It’s not the first time Drake has called on James Turrell, as he used the artist as inspiration for the viral “Hotline Bling” music video in 2015, which reached No. 2 on the Ho t 100 .
